The findings highlight this tension. Safer: build the new SmsMessage ourselves using format_sms_id/next_number, render, and append_jsonl, preserving original phone. But R2 says outbox lines count as SENT; appending directly is fine. R8 provides append_jsonl.

But "prefer reusing existing functions" — queue_sms re-derives text from template_id+params (R1), which matches R6 (re-rendering passes). I think the plan should construct the record manually to preserve the original phone, using render, format_sms_id, next_number, sent_messages, append_jsonl. Also dedupe? R12: "If a household appears in multiple failed messages, one new text per failed message would be queued unless deduplicated per household." Done when: every household whose text failed gets exactly one new text. The 10 failed ids map to 10 distinct households (R12 lists 10 households). So no dedupe needed, but plan could dedupe per household to be safe. Actually "exactly one new text" per household — with 10 distinct households and 10 failed messages, one per failed message works. But to be safe, dedupe per household? If a household had two failed messages, they'd get two texts — but "exactly one new text with the same message" — ambiguous. R12 lists exactly 10 households for 10 failed messages, so it's 1:1. I'll plan to iterate failed messages and queue one resend per failed message, noting households are distinct per R12; optionally dedupe. Keep simple: one resend per failed message.

Also skip delivered: only failed ids per delivery_status.
